title: MF-MOR: Multi-Fidelity Model Order Reduction for Many-Port Linear Systems in Chip Power Modeling
problem: Reducing systems with millions of nodes and tens of thousands of I/O ports is extremely difficult; existing projection-based MOR techniques offer only partial solutions for many-port systems.
motivation: Efficient model order reduction for 3DIC power modeling is critical for advanced package design and validation.
method: Multi-fidelity ML strategy combining aggressive port reduction followed by conventional MOR (PRIMA) for low-fidelity ROM, high-fidelity time-domain simulation for limited samples, compensation network trained to bridge gap, tensorized mapping technique capturing port correlations for efficient learning.
key_novelty: Multi-fidelity approach combining reduced-order model with learned compensation network for many-port systems.
contributions: Multi-fidelity MOR strategy for many-port linear systems
Tensorized mapping technique capturing port and transient correlations
Scalable approach for large-scale chip power modeling

metrics.other: Scalable and cost-effective, generalizable to different input waveforms

limitations: Limited numerical results provided; generalization to non-linear systems unclear.
